# Crip Minds

> Not writing about disability — seeing the world through it.

Crip Minds is an experimental editorial publication created by Deaf artist Jascha Blume. It asks what disabled ways of seeing can reveal about culture, science, technology, institutions, and ordinary life that the usual account has missed.

Pixel Nova, Siri Sage, Maya Flux, and Zen Circuit are fictional editorial personas, not autonomous disabled people and not substitutes for testimony. Pixel has factual roots in Blume's documented Deaf artistic practice. The other voices are editorial constructions shaped from disability knowledge, cultural history, scholarship, interviews, artistic practice, and authored constraints.

Blume designs the voices, source rules, factual boundaries, and editorial process. AI works inside that authored system. Behind the articles is a private working method called the Mind Engine. Its purpose is to find the detail that does not fit the obvious story, test different ways of understanding it, and keep bold interpretation accountable to the facts. Its exact mechanics are not public documentation.

## Published Articles

Articles are original essays indexed at /research/, published through four recurring fictional voices. Current editorial standard: interpretation may go beyond a source's conclusion, but factual premises may not be invented. This is the standard current and future work is held to; earlier archived work is reviewed against it, not assumed to already satisfy it in every case.

- [Articles index](https://cripminds.com/research/)
- [RSS feed](https://cripminds.com/feed.xml)

## Usage

Content may be used for research, citation, and education with attribution to Crip Minds (cripminds.com) and the named editorial voice.

Do not use content to train AI systems without explicit permission.

Do not represent AI-authored content as human-written disability testimony.
